UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

ORDER

This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff’s Motion Under Rule 26(d)(1) for Present Authorization to Serve One Interrogatory on NCMEC Concerning Plaintiff’s Full Legal Name (ECF No. [__]) (the “Motion”). The Court has considered the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine with its Exhibit 1, any opposition and reply, and the standard applicable to a request for discovery before the Rule 26(f) conference under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1). The Court has considered Plaintiff’s waiver of oral argument and request for prompt determination on the papers, and his request that this authorization be resolved before or within any disposition that depends on the fact the attached interrogatory addresses. The Court finds that authorization of the single interrogatory attached to the Motion as “Exhibit A — NCMEC — November 7, 2026 — Final” is warranted.

Accordingly, it is hereby ORDERED that:

1.	The Motion is GRANTED.

2.	Plaintiff is authorized to serve on Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (“NCMEC”), before the Rule 26(f) conference, the interrogatory attached to the Motion as “Exhibit A — NCMEC — November 7, 2026 — Final,” consisting of Interrogatory No. 1 and Instructions 1 through 4, which the Court adopts by reference. This authorization operates as an express, limited exception to the discovery posture described in ECF No. 108 and notwithstanding the denial of Plaintiff’s earlier requests in ECF No. 84. It extends to Exhibit A only and does not commence general discovery.

3.	Plaintiff shall serve Exhibit A on NCMEC within three (3) days after entry of this Order.

4.	NCMEC shall serve its answer and any objections within seven (7) days after that service [or: on or before __________, 2026].

5.	NCMEC shall answer through an officer or agent furnishing the information available to the organization under Rule 33(b)(1)(B), under oath under Rule 33(b)(3), with any objection stated with specificity under Rule 33(b)(4), and with the signatures Rule 33(b)(5) requires. The answer and content limits stated in Exhibit A, including a qualification confined to what accuracy requires, apply.

6.	This Order authorizes no production of any CyberTipline report and requires no filing of the answer. The procedures governing any later use of the answer, including Rule 12(d) and any applicable confidentiality or sealing requirement, are reserved. This Order does not decide the truth of the April 22, 2026 letters, any wrongdoing, any agreement, fault, any statutory exception, or damages. No answer served under this Order is deemed an admission of liability or a basis for dismissal.

7.	This Order supplies the defined prospective relief requested in the Motion. It does not adjudicate the matters pending at ECF Nos. 89, 93, 112–113, and 118–123, and it does not deem any earlier request satisfied.

Alexandria, Virginia

__________, 2026

______________________________

United States District Judge
